methodological_rigor.justification: The study triangulates its central claim (DNAPKcs/NHEJ as an immunotherapy-resistance node in SCLC) using a very large retrospective molecular profiling cohort (179,508 tumors across 24 types; 944 SCLC tumors for subtyping) together with mechanistic cell-line experiments and multiple in vivo models, including immunocompetent GEMM-derived tumors treated with DNAPKcs inhibition and anti-PD-L1 (Results Fig. 1; Methods: clinical cohort; Results Fig. 6–7). Mechanistic steps are supported by pathway readouts (p-STING/p-TBK1/p-IRF3 induction with NU7441 and reversal with STING inhibition; interferon/chemokine induction with STING-dependence) and functional immune-dependence experiments (STING knockdown abrogating immune infiltration/MHC-I effects; CD8 depletion reversing antitumor efficacy) (Results: STING inhibition and CD8 depletion sections). In vivo endpoints are tracked longitudinally and analyzed with linear mixed-effects regression models that account for repeated tumor-volume measures per mouse, which is appropriate for these growth-curve data (Methods: Statistics and reproducibility; Results figure legends). Limitations include reliance on retrospective observational associations for the human response/prognosis links (e.g., PRKDC-high vs low survival and IMpower133 stratification) and incomplete visibility in the normalized text on randomization/blinding procedures for all in vivo arms beyond explicit randomization noted in the CD8-depletion experiment (Results; Methods).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The manuscript addresses a high-need clinical setting (SCLC with modest immunotherapy benefit) and directly tests a therapeutically actionable strategy by combining DNAPKcs inhibition (NU7441) with anti-PD-L1 blockade in immunocompetent SCLC models, while also analyzing large human tumor profiling datasets and survival/response associations with PRKDC expression (Abstract; Results Fig. 1; Results Fig. 6–7). On the Oxford CEBM scale, the highest applicable evidence comes from the individual cohort-type analyses (e.g., SCLC survival curves by PRKDC expression in a 423-patient set and stratification of IMpower133 outcomes by PRKDC expression) rather than the preclinical experiments alone, supporting LoE 2b (Results Fig. 1G–I; Methods: retrospective de-identified cohort). The clinical relevance is very high because the proposed mechanism (cGAS/STING reactivation and immune infiltration) maps onto an established barrier in SCLC ("cold" TME with low T-cell infiltration/MHC-I) and the in vivo combinations are aligned with current checkpoint strategies (Introduction; Results Fig. 6–8). The main caveat is that therapeutic benefit is demonstrated preclinically and via biomarker correlations rather than a prospective, biomarker-stratified clinical intervention (Results; Discussion).

reporting_quality.justification: Because the paper includes substantial retrospective observational analyses linking PRKDC expression to outcomes and pathway signatures in real-world SCLC cohorts and trial datasets, STROBE is the closest applicable reporting standard for the clinical/associational component (Methods: clinical cohort; Results Fig. 1). The manuscript provides clear cohort sizes and key processing steps for transcriptome profiling (FFPE inclusion threshold, WTS pipeline, aligner/quantification tools) and reports statistical tests for clinical comparisons (e.g., Mann-Whitney U tests with P-values for subtype comparisons; log-rank/Cox analyses for survival) (Methods; Results Fig. 1 legend). For the preclinical work, figure legends consistently report n, dosing schedules, and analysis approaches (including mixed-effects models for tumor growth curves) and the Methods include ethics approvals and endpoint limits (Methods; Results Fig. 6–7 legends). Data/code availability in the normalized text is limited to references to supplementary tables and reporting summaries, without explicit repository links for processed data/code, so reproducibility is moderate rather than fully transparent (Methods: Supplementary Tables/Reporting summary references).

novelty_literature.justification: The paper proposes and supports a mechanistic bridge between NHEJ/DNAPKcs inhibition and activation of tumor-intrinsic cGAS/STING signaling in SCLC, including a pathway link through GSK3beta-mediated MYC degradation and downstream interferon/chemokine induction (Abstract; Results sections describing STING pathway activation and immune modulation). It extends beyond correlative observations by demonstrating STING-dependence (pharmacologic STING inhibition and STING knockdown reversing pathway activation and immune infiltration) and CD8-dependence for antitumor efficacy in vivo (Results: STING inhibition; Results: CD8 depletion). The integration of large-scale real-world tumor profiling (179,508 tumors) with subtype-specific SCLC analyses and preclinical combination therapy provides a broad evidentiary base that is more than incremental within the SCLC immunotherapy-resistance literature (Results Fig. 1; Results Fig. 6–8). However, the therapeutic concept is still preclinical and builds on established principles that DNA damage and innate sensing can modulate immunogenicity, so novelty is strong but not field-defining (Introduction; Discussion).

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript presents a coherent translational narrative from human tumor profiling and prognosis/response associations to mechanistic pathway studies and then to immunocompetent in vivo efficacy with checkpoint blockade (Abstract; Results order; Discussion). Methods include concrete parameters for key experimental components (WTS pipeline, subtyping rules, siRNA/shRNA conditions, dosing schedules) and the statistics section explains mixed-effects tumor-growth modeling, which helps interpretability (Methods: RNA WTS; Methods: Statistics and reproducibility). Figure legends (as preserved) are detailed and include sample sizes and statistical tests, enabling evaluation even without images in this normalized corpus (Results Fig. 1, 6–7 legends). Some passages contain grammatical repetition and minor wording issues (e.g., duplicated phrases, occasional typos), but overall clarity is good and the main claims are traceable to reported experiments (Results; Methods).

key_strengths: Large real-world molecular profiling analysis shows PRKDC is highly expressed in SCLC relative to other cancers and links PRKDC to survival/response stratifications in SCLC datasets (179,508 tumors; SCLC n = 944; Results Fig. 1).
Mechanistic evidence supports cGAS/STING pathway activation after DNAPKcs inhibition, including downstream IFN/chemokine induction and reversal with STING inhibition (Results: Fig. 3-related text).

In vivo efficacy is tested in immunocompetent SCLC GEMM models and is shown to be STING-dependent and CD8-dependent, strengthening causal interpretation for immune-mediated tumor control (Results Fig. 6–7).

Combination strategy with anti-PD-L1 aligns with clinical immunotherapy practice and is supported by longitudinal tumor-growth modeling using mixed-effects regression (Methods; Results figure legends).
key_concerns: Human outcome associations are retrospective and may be confounded; prospective biomarker-stratified clinical testing of DNAPKcs inhibition plus ICB is not presented (Methods: retrospective cohort; Results Fig. 1H–I).

Randomization/blinding procedures for animal allocation and outcome assessment are not consistently explicit in the normalized text across all in vivo experiments, which can affect internal validity (Methods/Results).

Data/code access details (e.g., public deposition of processed WTS outputs, analysis scripts, and model metadata) are not clearly specified in the normalized manuscript, limiting independent reproduction (Methods: Supplementary Tables/Reporting summary references).

Given the multi-arm, multi-endpoint nature of the work, clearer multiplicity-control and prespecified primary endpoints would further strengthen statistical interpretability, even though mixed-effects modeling is appropriate for growth curves (Methods: Statistics and reproducibility).
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study is clinically important for SCLC, supported by large-scale human profiling plus strong mechanistic and immune-dependence in vivo data; remaining gaps are mainly in prospective validation and reporting/transparency rather than core plausibility, making it suitable for Tier 2 with minor revisions.
